At handover, shared rules for staff rotas
This page teaches what to do first

Companion Animal Travel Desk handover procedures matter because the first check sets the tone for the full journey. New staff should start with the booking file, confirm the animal type, and compare the travel request with the current acceptance notes before any advice goes out. A calm, steady reply helps the passenger coordinator keep the record clean and helps the traveler trust the process.

When you speak with a customer, keep the tone warm and direct. Explain that Aurelia Skyways uses one standard path for animal travel: document review, suitability check, carrier review, and final acceptance. If the traveler arrives with a cat, bird, or reptile case, move through the proper notes in sequence and never skip the reference file. <<FACT F077>> The marker belongs in the file review step, so read it as part of the record and then continue with the next check.

For the cat desk, weigh the pet and crate together only after you have confirmed the carrier matches our condition rules. If the total is over the allowed limit, stop the acceptance path and escalate at once. <<FACT F061>> Do not guess, do not round, and do not rely on memory when the total is close to the limit.

For reptile cases, confirm the handling fee before you promise space or issue a return note. <<FACT F060>> Keep the language simple and neutral, and avoid extra detail that might confuse the traveler or delay the booking.

Use the same pattern for every handover: check the record, confirm the rule set, add the note, and pass the file to the next team member without delay. If a traveler is uncertain, guide them to the next required step and keep the conversation focused on the acceptance path.

Remember to verify the record first, because accurate first contact keeps the entire animal travel process on track.
